setup_summary.text: Q3 FY2026 (quarter ended 2026-09-27) revenue was $25.40B, +5.9% reported and +6.0% operational. Nine-month revenue was $74.77B, +7.4%.

GAAP Q3 net income was $210M (diluted EPS $0.09) versus $5.15B ($2.12). The drop is mostly a $5.5B charge for the proposed ovarian talc resolution and about $1.0B of acquired IPR&D for Firefly Bio. Nine-month EPS was $4.49 versus $8.94, and the prior period included a ~$7.0B talc reserve reversal.

Management's non-GAAP Q3 adjusted EPS was $2.59 (-7.5% y/y) and adjusted net earnings were $6.3B (-6.8%). Adjusted pretax margin fell to 30.2% from 35.2%. Innovative Medicine slid to 35.4% from 44.3% on Firefly IPR&D, Cell BioMedicines costs and mix. MedTech rose to 22.9% from 21.0% on tariff recoveries.

Innovative Medicine drove the quarter. Sales were $16.76B (+7.7% reported, +7.9% operational; US +11.1%), with STELARA a ~6.9-point drag on segment operational growth. MedTech grew 2.5% to $8.64B (US +4.8%, international +0.1%), which management said fell short of its own expectations.

Q3 gross margin was 68.1% versus 69.6%, on STELARA mix and higher CAPLYTA/Intra-Cellular amortization, partly offset by ~$0.2B of MedTech tariff recoveries. R&D was 18.3% of sales versus 15.3%, including Firefly. SM&A was flat at 24.7% of sales.

Management raised and tightened FY2026 operational sales growth guidance to 6.7%-7.1% (midpoint $100.7B). Reported growth is guided to 7.2%-7.6% (midpoint $101.2B) at a 1.15 average euro rate. Adjusted pretax margin is now guided down ~60bp (from -75bp in July) and free cash flow is guided to ~$21B.

Nine-month free cash flow was $15.12B (operating cash flow $18.85B less capex $3.73B) versus $14.23B a year earlier. Net debt was $27.4B at quarter-end. Management cited upcoming cash needs of ~$9.0B for talc, $3.2B of current bonds, ~$2.6B for the Sail acquisition option and ~$0.9B for opioid settlements.

Street positioning is constructive going into the print. Recent rating actions (Wells Fargo, Morgan Stanley, RBC, Leerink, Guggenheim, Citi) were all maintained Buy/Overweight/Outperform. The consensus target is $285.31 (+4.4% vs $273.20). JNJ beat in 3 of the last 4 quarters (average surprise +0.5%), and the average closing move on earnings is ±2.2%.

The next report is fiscal Q4 2026 on 2027-01-26 after the close, and the Q4 quarter should contain the 53rd week. Management's Enterprise Business Review on December 8 comes first and will set the 2027 outlook, so the EBR, not the print, is likely to reset the 2027 numbers.

last_reported.text: Q3 FY2026 revenue was $25.40B, +5.9% y/y. Q4 FY2025 revenue was $24.56B (derived).

consensus.text: Consensus revenue is $26.71B, implying +8.7% y/y against $24.56B.

view.text: Guided reported FY growth of 7.2%-7.6% less nine-month sales of $74.77B implies Q4 sales of ~$26.2B-$26.6B (+6.7% to +8.2% y/y, helped by the extra week). Consensus of $26.71B sits above the top of that range, so the bar looks slightly stretched unless guidance is conservative. JNJ's modest beat record (+0.5% average surprise) argues for modelling near the top of the range, not above consensus. Currency should be a Q4 headwind: nine-month currency was +1.4 points versus ~+0.5 points implied for the year.

view.text: Reported adjusted EPS is guided to $11.05-$11.15 for FY2026 (midpoint $11.10, +2.9%), with $0.64 of dilution from Firefly Bio and Cell BioMedicines. last_reported.text: Q3 Innovative Medicine sales were $16.76B (+7.7%, operational +7.9%). Q4 FY2025 is ~$15.76B (derived: FY $60.40B less nine months $44.64B).

view.text: The quarterly operational growth rate has been ~8% in Q3 despite a ~7-point STELARA drag. TREMFYA (+68%), DARZALEX (+15.6%), CARVYKTI, RYBREVANT, SPRAVATO and CAPLYTA are the offsets. Headwinds are US OPSUMIT generics (first full quarter) and SIMPONI biosimilars. Q4 should hold high-single-digit operational growth plus the extra week.

last_reported.text: Q3 MedTech sales were $8.64B (+2.5%, all operational). Q4 FY2025 is ~$8.80B (derived: FY $33.79B less nine months $24.99B).

view.text: This is the segment with the most estimate risk. Management guided to a Q4 return to growth in Surgery and improvement in Abiomed, citing a stable procedure environment and a Q4 VARIPULSE Pro approval. Against that, Surgery was -1.0% operational, the Middle East disruption has widened, and EP growth was 4.4% in Q3 while Abbott's EP grew double digits.

last_reported.text: Q3 STELARA sales were $716M, -54.4% (operational -54.0%). Nine-month sales were $2,112M versus $4,848M. The call transcript's '-5.4%' appears to be a transcription error.

view.text: The Q4 FY2025 base is ~$1.23B (derived: FY $6,078M less nine months $4,848M). H1 2026 sales averaged ~$0.70B a quarter and Q3 was $0.72B, so the decline is stabilizing in dollars. The y/y drag on growth should shrink versus Q3's ~4.2 points of worldwide operational growth.

last_reported.text: Q3 TREMFYA sales were $2,396M (+68.3%). Nine-month sales were $6,050M.

view.text: The Q4 FY2025 base is ~$1.59B (derived: FY $5,155M less nine months $3,566M). The comparison is tougher than Q3's, so y/y growth should decelerate from 68% even if dollar sales keep rising on the IBD launch. Management cites share gains of four points in both UC and Crohn's and a $10B+ franchise ambition.

last_reported.text: Q3 Pulmonary Hypertension sales were $897M (-19.5%). OPSUMIT/OPSYNVI was $372M (-35.7%) after US generic entry late in Q2.

view.text: Q4 FY2025 bases are ~$1.18B for PH and ~$0.64B for OPSUMIT (derived). Q4 is the second full quarter of US generics, and European OPSUMIT and UPTRAVI generics are flagged for 2027. Expect a similar or larger y/y decline.

last_reported.text: Q3 adjusted pretax margin was 30.2% versus 35.2%. Innovative Medicine was 35.4% and MedTech 22.9%.

view.text: FY adjusted operating margin is guided down ~60bp, including a 150bp hit from the Firefly and Cell BioMedicines deals plus the 53rd week and the US-government access agreement. With the deal charges already taken in Q3, the Q4 y/y margin comparison should be less negative. Watch the MedTech tariff-recovery contribution (~$0.2B in Q3), which may not repeat.

view.text: The FY effective tax rate is guided to 17.0%-17.5%. That is not on the same basis as the GAAP nine-month rate, but it signals a higher Q4 rate than the GAAP year-to-date figure. Net interest expense is guided to $150M-$200M.

view.text: The ~$21B FY FCF guide less $15.12B year-to-date implies Q4 FCF of ~$5.9B. Capex is running +24.6% y/y, and cash outflows for the talc settlement are expected to start from the ~$9.0B reserve (about half is current).

since_filing.text: Abbott (reported 2026-10-21) grew Q3 worldwide Medical Devices 7.8% comparable, led by double-digit Electrophysiology and Rhythm Management, and reaffirmed EPS guidance; its shares fell on the day. Abbott's H1 EP growth was 13.0% ex-FX. Against JNJ's Q3 EP growth of 4.4% operational, this suggests continued PFA share pressure on JNJ's cardiovascular franchise (a peer proxy, not JNJ data).

Merck (reported 2026-10-29) grew Q3 sales 5% to $18.1B, beat adjusted EPS ($2.49 vs $2.09 consensus) and raised its profit outlook, citing launches and oncology strength. This is a constructive read for large-cap pharma demand and pricing into JNJ's Q4.

Leerink maintained Buy with a $272 target on 2026-10-28, which is below the current $273.20 share price. The consensus target of $285.31 implies only +4.4% upside. The stock closed at $258.93 on Oct 20, so it is up ~5.5% since the Q3 print, which leaves less room for a Q4 shortfall.

TIKR (2026-10-29) frames JNJ as up 42% in a year at ~24x earnings that barely grow until 2028 (consensus normalized EPS ~$13.92), and calls the December 8 Enterprise Business Review the real test. That makes the 2027 outlook, not Q4 itself, the main stock catalyst before the print.

The talc status should not be overstated. The TIKR article (2026-10-29) says JNJ moved to settle ovarian talc claims. The 10-Q (filed 2026-10-21) says the resolution is a proposal conditioned on at least 95% claimant participation, with a $5.5B commitment and a ~$9.0B total reserve. No source shows the 95% threshold has been met, and the filing is the more reliable source.

Policy backdrop: IQVIA's Q3 call (2026-10-27) describes large-pharma pauses over IRA, MFN and tariffs as easing, though the overhang remains. A Motley Fool piece (2026-10-24) notes nine drugmakers signed US pricing deals for tariff exemptions. JNJ's own voluntary agreements with the US government are cited in its filings.

Legal items in the 10-Q (filed 2026-10-21): the Third Circuit dismissed the insurers' appeal of the Imerys settlement order in October 2026. Summary judgment was granted for JNJ in the REMICADE/SIMPONI ARIA qui tam, with the relator's appeal deadline on October 30 (outcome unknown). A new Lupin ERLEADA patent suit was also filed in October.

Leadership: the call names Tom Cavanagh as Worldwide Chairman, Innovative Medicine and thanks Jennifer Taubert on her exit. The 10-K (2026-02-11) lists Taubert in that role, so the call is the newer item. The sources do not give the timing of the handover.

Two call-versus-filing inconsistencies should be treated with care. The call says STELARA fell 5.4%, but the 10-Q shows -54.4% ($716M vs $1,570M), so the filing governs. The call attributes Q3 deal expense to Firefly Bio and Cell BioMedicines, while the 10-Q names the Sail Biomedicines collaboration ($0.3B option premium) and never mentions Cell BioMedicines. The sources do not reconcile these.
The next regular quarterly dividend is $1.34 per share, payable December 8 to holders of record November 24. JNJ usually raises the dividend in Q1; the January 2026 declaration was $1.30.

key_debates.question: Was the Q3 MedTech shortfall transitory?

bull.text: Management says the weakness was concentrated outside the US and in Abiomed, that US MedTech grew almost 5%, and that procedures are deferred, not lost. It says Europe EP is back to double-digit growth with VARIPULSE Pro and expects Surgery to return to growth and the segment to improve in Q4.

bear.text: Q3 MedTech grew only 2.5% and international was +0.1%. Surgery was -1.0% and the Middle East headwind has widened to more countries. EP grew 4.4% versus double digits at Abbott, and Abiomed fell 1.5% operationally.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Q4 MedTech operational growth versus Q3's 2.5%, EP growth against Abbott's pace, Abiomed's US trend, ex-US Surgery, and any quantification of the Middle East and VBP effects.

key_debates.question: Is the Q4 consensus bar too high relative to guidance?

bull.text: JNJ beat in 3 of the last 4 quarters, Q3 operational growth beat consensus per management, and the FY guide was raised. The extra week should help Q4 sales growth.

bear.text: Guided reported FY growth implies Q4 sales of ~$26.2B-$26.6B, below the $26.71B consensus. The +40.6% consensus EPS growth is measured against a GAAP base, so the comparison is unreliable.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Where Q4 sales land against the guide-implied range and consensus, and whether consensus resets after the December 8 EBR.

key_debates.question: Can Innovative Medicine outgrow rising loss-of-exclusivity pressure into 2027?

bull.text: TREMFYA grew 68%, oncology 17%, and ICOTYDE, INLEXZO and RYBREVANT are ramping. Management reiterates a path to double-digit growth by the end of the decade without acquisitions.

bear.text: STELARA is still a ~4-point drag, OPSUMIT has US generics, and SIMPONI biosimilars are in Europe with a possible US entrant. UPTRAVI, XARELTO and European OPSUMIT generics are flagged for 2027. An analyst read of management's 2027 comments is ~5.4% reported growth and the Firefly/Cell deals add $1.36 of EPS dilution.

key_debates.what_settles_it: The December 8 Enterprise Business Review 2027 outlook, ICOTYDE launch data (sales, PsA, ASCEND), and SIMPONI biosimilar timing.

key_debates.question: Is talc largely behind the company?

bull.text: The ovarian docket resolution is priced at $5.5B and the reserve is now ~$9.0B. Favorable MDL rulings and plaintiffs' withdrawal of causation experts in the first bellwether matters helped, and in October 2026 the Third Circuit dismissed the insurers' appeal of the Imerys settlement order.

bear.text: The deal is conditional on at least 95% claimant participation. The mesothelioma docket is unaffected, about 76,500 plaintiffs remain, and the securities class action is in expert discovery. Roughly half of the $9.0B reserve is current, so cash out is near term.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Confirmation that the 95% participation threshold is met, any change to the accrual, and the timing of payments.

MedTech is low-single-digit with continued international softness. Adjusted EPS is near the FY guide and the stock reaction stays inside historical ranges.

triggers: No change to FY free cash flow of ~$21B

scenarios.name: bear

description.text: MedTech weakness persists (Middle East disruption, China VBP, PFA competitive pressure, Abiomed volumes) and generics erode Innovative Medicine faster than modelled. Q4 sales fall short of the $26.71B consensus. A weak 2027 outlook at the December 8 Enterprise Business Review, or a shortfall against the 95% claimant participation condition on the talc resolution, compounds the move after a ~5.5% rise from the $258.93 close on October 20 to $273.20.

triggers: 2027 growth framework near or below ~5% reported
Talc participation threshold missed or accrual increased

claim.text: MedTech execution and geopolitics: the Middle East disruption now affects ordering and tenders across a wider group of countries. China VBP is expanding, PFA competition is intensifying in Asia-Pacific, and Abiomed volumes fell after an ex-US high-risk PCI study. Management called Q3 below its own standard and has not quantified the impacts.

Loss of exclusivity is broadening: STELARA biosimilars (~4.2 points of Q3 worldwide growth), OPSUMIT US generics from late Q2, SIMPONI biosimilars in Europe with a US entrant possible (preliminary injunction appealed), BIOCAD's at-risk daratumumab biosimilar launch in Russia, and 2027 generic risk for UPTRAVI, XARELTO and European OPSUMIT.

Talc: the $5.5B ovarian resolution requires at least 95% claimant participation. The ~$9.0B reserve (about half current) is a sizeable near-term cash call. The mesothelioma docket and the securities class action are unresolved.

Q4 estimate risk: consensus revenue of $26.71B exceeds the sales implied by reported guidance, and the 53rd week and a higher FY tax rate (17.0%-17.5% versus 14.0% GAAP year-to-date) complicate the Q4 comparison.

Drug pricing, international reference pricing, IRA negotiation (ERLEADA selected for 2028), 340B policy changes and tariffs remain open policy risks; the 10-Q says the company may be further impacted by tariffs. Q3 MedTech included ~$0.2B of tariff recoveries.
Orthopaedics separation: costs were $0.4B in Q3 and $0.7B year to date, and completion by mid-2027 remains subject to execution and conditions. Management is leaning toward a spin.

Capital commitments and dilution: ~$2.6B Sail acquisition option, $3.2B of current bonds, ~$9.0B talc and $0.9B opioid obligations. The Firefly/Cell BioMedicines deals dilute 2027 adjusted EPS by $1.36. Net debt was $27.4B.
Currency: the guide uses a 1.15 average euro rate against a 1.12 spot, and management said that if the current spot rate holds into next year, currency could be a headwind.

questions_for_management.question: What is the Q4 and 2027 growth cadence for MedTech, and can you quantify the Middle East and China VBP impacts on Surgery and EP?

why.text: MedTech grew 2.5% in Q3 (international +0.1%). Management guided to improvement in Q4 but declined to quantify the Middle East and VBP effects.

questions_for_management.question: How much does the 53rd week add to Q4 sales and expenses, and how should we reconcile consensus Q4 revenue of $26.71B with the guide-implied $26.2B-$26.6B?

why.text: FY2026 is a 53-week year and guidance reflects the cost of the 53rd week. The $101.2B reported sales guidance midpoint less nine-month sales of $74.77B implies Q4 of about $26.4B, below the $26.71B consensus.

questions_for_management.question: What is the Q4 adjusted EPS bridge (deal charges, tax rate, interest) behind the $11.05-$11.15 FY guide?

why.text: Nine-month adjusted EPS is not in the filings, and the FY tax guide of 17.0%-17.5% implies a higher Q4 rate than the 14.0% GAAP year-to-date rate.

questions_for_management.question: Please reconcile the Cell BioMedicines collaboration cited on the call with the Sail Biomedicines agreement disclosed in the 10-Q.

why.text: The call ties the $0.64 EPS dilution to Firefly and Cell BioMedicines, while the 10-Q names Sail ($0.3B option premium) and never mentions Cell BioMedicines.

questions_for_management.question: Where do talc participation levels stand against the 95% threshold, and when will payments start?

why.text: The $5.5B resolution is conditional on at least 95% participation, and about half of the ~$9.0B reserve is current.

questions_for_management.question: How do you expect SIMPONI, OPSUMIT and UPTRAVI erosion to affect 2027 growth, and is the ~5% reported growth reading of your 2027 comments accurate?

why.text: An analyst inferred ~5.4% reported 2027 growth, and the filing flags 2027 generic entrants and SIMPONI biosimilars.

questions_for_management.question: Can you share ICOTYDE's net sales run-rate and the timing of the PsA and ASCEND readouts?

why.text: ICOTYDE is a key growth driver, but sales were not disclosed, and management said they would be next year.

questions_for_management.question: What are the vehicle, timing and stranded-cost expectations for the DePuy Synthes spin?

why.text: Management now leans toward a spin by mid-2027, and separation costs reached $0.7B year to date.

Nine-month adjusted EPS and the Q4 FY2025 adjusted EPS are not provided, so Q4 adjusted EPS implied by the FY guide cannot be derived, and the consensus basis (adjusted vs GAAP) is unconfirmed. The consensus-implied +40.6% EPS growth uses a GAAP base.
Company has not quantified the 53rd-week contribution to Q4 revenue or costs, nor the Q4 operational growth implied by guidance; the ~100bp extra-week figure comes only from an analyst's question.
No options-implied move or whisper EPS is available (the report date is 86 days away); only the ±2.2% historical average move.
Management has not reconciled Cell BioMedicines (call) with Sail Biomedicines (10-Q); the dollar size of the Cell BioMedicines deal is not disclosed.
Status of talc participation against the 95% threshold, and whether the relator appealed the REMICADE/SIMPONI ARIA summary judgment by October 30, are not in the sources.
An IRS-dispute quote attributed to 'CFO John Murphy' in the 24/7 Wall St. dividend article (N.18) does not match JNJ's CFO (Joseph Wolk) and appears to refer to another company; it was excluded.
Exact timing of the Cavanagh/Taubert leadership transition is not given.
Post-Q3 consensus revisions for Q4 are not available; M.01 may predate the guidance raise.
The 2027 outlook will only be provided at the December 8 Enterprise Business Review, after this note.
